question: Should OpenClaw sponsor the core Claws lifecycle and allow this managed-workspace-file slice to proceed as part of the ordered implementation stack?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but it creates durable package, workspace, provenance, and future removal/update contracts whose acceptance cannot be inferred from tests or patch quality.

options.title: Pause for RFC acceptance
options.body: Keep this protected draft open and do not land the stack until the Claws RFC is formally accepted or narrowed.

options.title: Sponsor and sequence landing
options.body: Approve the product direction, require current-head live proof, and then review and land the dependent slices in order.

options.title: Decline the core lifecycle
options.body: Reject the core direction and close the associated implementation stack rather than maintaining an unsupported persistent surface.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep this protected draft open and do not land the stack until the Claws RFC is formally accepted or narrowed.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans canonical shared state, core lifecycle ownership, and the security boundary for package-controlled agent workspaces.
